script_text:
INT. LUXURY APARTMENT - DAY

RAY (40s, slick, overconfident) paces in front of a floor-to-
ceiling window, iPhone pressed to his ear. A McLaren 720S sits
parked visibly on the street below.

                    RAY
          Tell Nike we want the deal by Friday.
          If they walk, Adidas is already circling.

He hangs up, pours a drink, and grabs the remote. The TV plays
a clip that looks unmistakably like a scene from Breaking Bad --
a man in a yellow hazmat suit cooking in an RV.

                    RAY (CONT'D)
          (to himself)
          Every empire starts with one good batch.

His assistant, DENISE (30s), enters holding a Starbucks cup with
the logo clearly visible.

                    DENISE
          Ray, legal called. They said the script
          references "the Batman voice" one too many
          times. Might want to cut that.

                    RAY
          Fine. Change it to "some superhero voice."
          Nobody'll notice.

Denise sets a folder on the table. On top: a photo of a man who
looks exactly like Elon Musk, unlabeled, mid-speech.

                    DENISE
          Also -- the soundtrack list still has three
          unlicensed Beatles songs on it.

                    RAY
          We'll deal with it in post.

FADE OUT.

copyright_risks.content: The TV plays a clip that looks unmistakably like a scene from Breaking Bad -- a man in a yellow hazmat suit cooking in an RV.
copyright_risks.description: Visual and descriptive reference to a specific, iconic scene from a copyrighted television series ('Breaking Bad'). This would require a synchronization license and potentially a master use license for the visual clip itself. Fair use is unlikely to apply for a direct, recognizable clip.
copyright_risks.suggested_fix: Obtain a license from AMC/Sony Pictures Television. Alternatively, create a generic 'TV show' clip that is clearly not 'Breaking Bad' or any other recognizable show.
copyright_risks.clearance_action: Contact AMC/Sony Pictures Television for licensing.

copyright_risks.content: the soundtrack list still has three unlicensed Beatles songs on it.
copyright_risks.description: Use of copyrighted musical compositions and master recordings by The Beatles without proper licensing. This requires both a synchronization license (for the composition) and a master use license (for the specific recording). Beatles songs are notoriously expensive and difficult to license.
copyright_risks.suggested_fix: Obtain synchronization and master use licenses for each song. Alternatively, replace with licensed library music or original compositions.
copyright_risks.clearance_action: Contact Sony Music Publishing (for compositions) and Apple Corps Ltd./Universal Music Group (for master recordings) for licensing.
